You ask for more time. You request more meetings. You raise new concerns about text you have not even read. And you keep doing that until the legislative window closes on its own. The banks discovered this strategy three months ago — and are executing it perfectly. Scott Besant, the US Treasury Secretary, just told Congress directly, the Clarity Act is not a crypto issue — it is a dollar issue. Passing it secures the dollar as the global reserve currency. Failing it hands that position to someone else. And the banks lobbying to kill it are the same banks that profit most from dollar dominance. They are not protecting the dollar. They are protecting themselves. Let me give you the precise picture of what the delay strategy actually looks like in practice, because it is more sophisticated and more damaging than most coverage acknowledges. Senator Tom Tillis, one of the key Clarity Act negotiators, has announced the markup will not happen in April. It is being pushed to May. The week of May 11th is now the earliest possible window. Meanwhile, the North Carolina Bank's Association, one of the most active bank lobbying groups in the country, has made Senator Tillis' office the specific target of a coordinated pressure campaign. Banks are submitting formal comments to the OCC arguing against stable coin yield provisions. And, critically, some of the banks raising objections haven not even seen the compromised texts they are objecting to. They are opposing language they have not read. That is not policy disagreement, that is a delay operation. And it is working exactly as designed. So, here is the question that should reframe everything about how you think about this situation. If Scott Besant has publicly told Congress that the Clarity Act is essential to securing the dollar as the global reserve currency, and the banks delaying it are the same institutions that profit most from that dollar dominance, what is the actual endgame of their delay strategy? And what happens to XRP, specifically, when the Clarity Act passes despite the delay. That is what we are mapping today. The delay strategy's precise mechanics, Besant's specific Congressional Testimony, the Loomis Ultimatum, Coinbase's Clarity Act position, the OCC Genius Act rulemaking, and why the Clarity Act passing transforms XRP's legal status in a way that changes institutional deployment at full scale. This is the Calm Analyst. No rage about the banks, no panic about the timeline. What I do on this channel is take the documented legislative record, the verified statements from the people inside the process, and the structural implications for XRP and read them precisely, without the emotional overlay. Let's get into it. Let me now map Scott Besson's congressional testimony precisely, because the specific framing he used elevates the Clarity Act, beyond a crypto industry issue, into a national security and monetary policy issue. Bessant told the Senate Committee directly that when the United States leads in best practices, safety and soundness in the financial world, whether banking, securities or digital assets, it is essential for several reasons. First, US leadership over the long term secures the primacy of the dollar as the global reserve currency. Second, US best practices emanate to the rest of the world, pulling other nations frameworks toward American standards, rather than toward chinese European, or other competing frameworks. He specifically identified crypto as an important future payment rail, not a speculative asset class, but core financial infrastructure. And he stated explicitly that the United States must be the payments leader in the world as it is the technological leader Read those statements together. The Treasury Secretary is not saying crypto is interesting, he is saying crypto is the next generation of dollar infrastructure. And the Clarity Act is the legislation that formally integrates that infrastructure into the U.S. financial system, on American terms, under American oversight, with American anti money laundering and KYC requirements. The banks lobbying against this legislation are not protecting America's financial interests. They are protecting their own revenue streams. Correspondent banking – the system through which large banks charge fees to move money across borders – generates hundreds of billions in annual revenue for the institutions that control it. XRP based on-demand liquidity directly threatens that revenue by making the correspondent banking intermediary unnecessary. The bank's understand this. Their delay strategy is not about protecting depositors it is about protecting correspondent banking margins. But that's not even the most urgent piece of this picture what senator Cynthia Lummis just said publicly and the specific language she chose reveals exactly how close the breaking point actually is let me now address senator Lummis public statement because it is the most honest assessment of where the Clarity Act actually stands that any legislator has made. Lummis stated, I am not going to let my colleagues sacrifice substantive and good progress in futile pursuit of a perfect bill that will never come. The offshore risk is real and our window is closing. It is time to finally get this done. A sitting US Senator who has devoted years to crypto-legislation and who is not running for re-election, making this her legacy, has publicly declared that a perfect bill will never come. She is not frustrated. She is drawing a line. She is telling her colleagues that the standard of perfection the banks are demanding is NOT a negotiating position. It is a permanent obstruction strategy designed to ensure the bill never reaches the floor. The Digital Chamber of Commerce sent a formal letter to Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, noting that 270 days have passed since the House passed the Clarity Act. More than 120 organizations from across the digital-asset ecosystem have formally urged the community to move forward immediately. The legislative window, as Patrick Whitmore identified, closes at August recess. And the markup has now been pushed from April to May, with the week of May 11 as the earliest possible date. The math is not comfortable. After the markup, the bill must go to the Senate floor, it must be reconciled with the House version, the reconcile bill must pass both chambers, and it must receive presidential signature, all before August recess. The Reconcile Bill must pass both Chambers, and it must receive Presidential signature. All before August Recess. That sequence requires every step to move without further delay. And the Banks are still pushing for more time to socialize the stablecoin yield compromise with banking stakeholders who have not even read the text. And the absence of statutory codification creates the specific legal risk that Besant identified in his Congressional testimony. Changing it would require a new Act of Congress, not a new SEC Director, not a new CFTC Rule, an Act of Congress! That is the legal durability that the current guidance does not provide – and that legal durability is precisely what US banks, ETF issuers, and large-scale institutions are waiting for before deploying XRP at full scale. Let me now address two developments that are happening simultaneously with the Clarity Act delay- because they tell you something important about the direction of travel regardless of the markup timeline. The office of the Cobtroller of the currency has confirmed it issued a proposed rule to implement the Genius Act, the stable coin legislation that passed last year. This is the formal start of a national regulatory framework for payment stable coins. Stable coin issuers will operate under a clear federal framework, OCC-supervised banks will fall under parts of the custody rules and the US is moving toward formally regulated digital dollars regardless of what happens to the clarity act markup in May first it demonstrates that the regulatory direction is irreversible even if the clarity act is delayed the broader digital asset regulatory framework is advancing through multiple channels simultaneously. Second, it creates an incentive for banks to engage constructively with the Clarity Act rather than delay it indefinitely. Because the longer they delay, the more the regulatory framework is being set by agencies like the OCC rather than negotiated through legislation where banks have more leverage. Coinbase's head of policy, Paul Brewal, made a specific public statement that deserves precise attention. He said, Either you are for clarity or you are against rewards. You cannot support both sides. The fight over rewards is now a direct test of whether lawmakers actually want real crypto clarity or a watered down version that protects banks. That statement frames The Clarity Act correctly. The stable coin yield debate is not a technical disagreement about financial stability. It is a proxy battle over whether the new financial system will be designed to benefit consumers through yield on digital dollar products, or to protect banks, by maintaining the model, where banks capture the interest spread and pay depositors nothing. Besant addressed this directly. The White House's own economic analysis showed no evidence of deposit flight since the genius act passed. Savings account deposits have actually increased. The banks are not protecting depositors. They are protecting the spread. Let me bring the complete picture together. The delay strategy is documented and operational. Banks are opposing Clarity Act texts they have not read, targeting Senator Tillis with coordinated pressure campaigns and is documented and operational. Banks are opposing Clarity Act texts, they have not read. Targeting Senator Tillis with coordinated pressure campaigns and submitting formal OCC comments designed to run the clock past the August recess deadline. Scott Besant has told Congress directly that the Clarity Act is a dollar issue, That passing it secures dollar reserve currency status and failing it hands that position to someone else. Senator Lemmus has publicly declared that the perfect bill will never come and that the window is closing. 270 days have passed since the House passed the bill. The LCC is moving forward with Genius Act implementation regardless, and Coinbase has drawn a clear line. Clarity or rewards? Not both. For XRP, the clarity Act transforms the current Judicial and Regulatory Commodity classifications into Permanent Federal Law. That transformation is the specific legal event that US banks with the largest balance sheets are waiting for before deploying it at full institutional scale, not SEC guidance, congressional statute. The banks executing the delay strategy understand this better than anyone because what they are delaying is not a crypto bill. They are delaying the moment when XRP becomes legally untouchable by any future administration that tries to reverse it. That is what $1.43 does not reflect, and that is what the August window is actually about. I'll see you in the next one.
